title: Brauer–Manin Obstruction for Rationally Connected Varieties
exact_target: For a rationally connected variety over a number field, do the Brauer compatibility conditions account for every failure of rational points to exist or approximate local solutions?

sources.citation: Olivier Wittenberg, "Rational points and zero-cycles on rationally connected varieties over number fields," arXiv:1604.08543; Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 97.2 (2018), 597-635.

J.-L. Colliot-Th\'el\`ene and A. N. Skorobogatov, \emph{Good reduction of the Brauer--Manin obstruction}, Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 365 (2013), 579--590; Lemmas 1.1 and 1.3, \S1 and Theorem 3.1.

Yonatan Harpaz and Olivier Wittenberg, \emph{On the fibration method for zero-cycles and rational points}, Annals of Mathematics 183 (2016), 229--295; Theorems 1.3, 1.5--1.6, Conjecture 9.1 and Corollary 9.25.

Nguyen Manh Linh, \emph{On the descent conjecture for rational points and zero-cycles}, Journal of the Institute of Mathematics of Jussieu 25(1) (2026), 515--563, published online 19 November 2025; Theorem A and \S3.4.
Yisheng Tian, \emph{A Simpler Approach to a Descent Conjecture of Wittenberg}, arXiv:2604.08146 (2026), consulted HTML version, abstract and Theorem 1.4.
